nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition and $S \subseteq G$. Two elements $x, y \in G$ are adjacent in the distinct link graph of $S$ if $x \ne y$ and there is some $s \in S$, different from both $x$ and $y$, with $x + y = s$, $x + s = y$ or $y + s = x$. In an abelian group this says exactly that $\{x, y, s\}$ is a distinct Schur triple for some $s \in S$. In the paper's graph $L^*_S[B]$ with vertex set $B$, these are…
nodes.title: Edges of the distinct link graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition and $S \subseteq G$. An element $x \in G$ carries a loop in the distinct link graph of $S$ if there are distinct $s, s' \in S$, both different from $x$, with $s + s' = x$, $x + s = s'$ or $x + s' = s$. In an abelian group this says exactly that $\{x, s, s'\}$ is a distinct Schur triple for some distinct $s, s' \in S$.
nodes.title: Loops of the distinct link graph

nodes.summary: For a subset $F$ of a set $G$ with an addition, this is the number of ordered pairs $(x, y)$ with $x, y \in F$ such that $x$, $y$ and $x + y$ are pairwise distinct and $x + y \in F$, that is, the number of ordered distinct Schur triples $(x, y, x + y)$ in $F$. If there are infinitely many such pairs, the value is $0$ by convention.
nodes.title: Number of distinct Schur triples

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$ and let $k$ be a natural number with $p = 3k + 2$. If $A \subseteq G$ is sum-free and $|A| > \left(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3(p + 1)}\right)|G|$, then there is a group homomorphism $\psi : G \to \mathbb{Z}_p$ with $\psi(a) \in \{k + 1, \dots, 2k + 1\}$ for every $a \in A$, where $\mathbb{Z}_p$ is identified with $\{0, 1, \dots, p - 1\}$.
nodes.title: Green–Ruzsa structure lemma

nodes.summary: For every real $\delta > 0$ there is a natural number $n_0$ such that every finite abelian group $G$ of order $n \ge n_0$ has a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $G$ with the following properties: (i) each $F \in \mathcal{F}$ contains at most $\delta n^2$ ordered distinct Schur triples $(x, y, x + y)$; (ii) every distinct sum-free subset of $G$ is contained in some $F \in \mathcal{F}$; (iii)…
nodes.title: Container lemma

nodes.summary: For every set $G$ with an addition and all $S, B \subseteq G$, the empty set is an independent set of the distinct link graph $L^*_S[B]$.
nodes.title: The empty set is independent in the distinct link graph

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition and let $S, B, I \subseteq G$. The set $I$ is an independent set of the distinct link graph $L^*_S[B]$ (the graph on vertex set $B$ given by the edges and loops of the distinct link graph of $S$) if $I \subseteq B$, no element of $I$ carries a loop, and no two elements of $I$ are adjacent.
nodes.title: Independent sets of the distinct link graph

nodes.summary: For every set $G$ with an addition, every sum-free subset of $G$ is distinct sum-free.
nodes.title: Sum-free sets are distinct sum-free

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition. A subset $S \subseteq G$ is distinct sum-free if there are no pairwise distinct $x, y, z \in S$ with $x + y = z$, that is, if $S$ contains no distinct Schur triple.
nodes.title: Distinct sum-free sets

nodes.summary: For every set $G$ with an addition, the empty subset of $G$ is sum-free.
nodes.title: The empty set is sum-free

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition. A subset $S \subseteq G$ is sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$, where $x = y$ is allowed; that is, $S$ contains no Schur triple $x + y = z$ with $x, y, z \in S$.
nodes.title: Sum-free set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite set and $p$ a natural number. Then $G$ is of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$ if and only if $p$ is prime, $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, $p$ divides $|G|$, and $p \le q$ for every prime $q$ with $q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ that divides $|G|$.
nodes.title: Characterization of type I(p)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite set and $p$ a natural number. $G$ is of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$ if $p$ is the smallest prime with $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ dividing $|G|$: that is, $p$ is prime, $p \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, $p$ divides $|G|$, and $p \le q$ for every prime $q$ with $q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ that divides $|G|$.
nodes.title: Groups of type I(p)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition. For every finite subset $S \subseteq G$, the largest size of a sum-free subset of $S$ is at most $|S|$.
nodes.title: Trivial bound on sum-free subsets

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $n$, and let $\mu(G)$ be the largest size of a sum-free subset of $G$. If $G$ is of type $\mathrm{I}(p)$ for a natural number $p$, then $\mu(G) = n\left(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3p}\right)$. If no prime $q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ divides $n$ and $3 \mid n$ (type $\mathrm{II}$), then $\mu(G) = n/3$. If no prime $q \equiv 2 \pmod 3$ divides $n$ and $3 \nmid n$ (type $\mathrm{III}$),…
nodes.title: Diananda–Yap and Green–Ruzsa theorem

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition and $S \subseteq G$. Write $\mu(S)$ for the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$ of the sizes of the finite sum-free subsets of $S$ (sets $T$ with $x + y \notin T$ for all $x, y \in T$), taken to be $0$ if these sizes are unbounded. For finite $S$ this is the largest size of a sum-free subset of $S$, and $\mu(G)$ is the value for $S = G$.
nodes.title: Size of a largest sum-free subset

nodes.title: Sharp lower bound on maximal distinct sum-free sets

nodes.summary: Write $f^*_{\max}(G)$ for the number of maximal distinct sum-free subsets of an abelian group $G$. nodes.title: Maximal distinct sum-free sets in groups of even order

There is a natural number $C$ such that for every real $\eta > 0$ there is $n_0$ with the following property. nodes.title: Sharp upper bound on maximal distinct sum-free sets

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a set with an addition. The number $f^*_{\max}(G)$ is the number of subsets of $G$ that are maximal, with respect to inclusion, among the distinct sum-free subsets of $G$, and it is $0$ if there are infinitely many such subsets. Here $S \subseteq G$ is distinct sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$ such that $x$, $y$ and $x + y$ are pairwise distinct.
nodes.title: Number of maximal distinct sum-free sets

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph, let $T$ be a set of vertices of $\Gamma$, let $n \ge 1$ and $D \ge 1$ be integers, and let $k$ be a real number. Suppose that the graph $\Gamma'$ obtained from $\Gamma$ by deleting $T$ is triangle-free, has $n$ vertices and has at least $n/2 + k$ edges, and that $\Gamma$ has maximum degree $\Delta(\Gamma) \le D$. nodes.title: Almost triangle-free bound

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, $n + k$ edges for an integer $k$, and maximum degree $\Delta \ge 1$. Then the number $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ of maximal independent sets of $\Gamma$ satisfies $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma) \le 3^{\Delta/13} \cdot 3^{n/3 - k/(13\Delta)}$.
nodes.title: Liu–Sharifzadeh stability bound

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 1$ be a real number and let $\Gamma$ be a finite graph with $n$ vertices, minimum degree $\delta(\Gamma)$ and maximum degree $\Delta(\Gamma) \le k\,\delta(\Gamma)$, and put $b = \sqrt{\delta(\Gamma)}$. Then the number $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ of maximal independent sets of $\Gamma$ satisfies…
nodes.title: Balogh–Liu–Sharifzadeh–Treglown bound

nodes.summary: For a graph $\Gamma$, $\mathrm{mis}(\Gamma)$ is the number of maximal independent sets of $\Gamma$, that is, of sets of pairwise non-adjacent vertices that are not properly contained in another such set; it is $0$ if there are infinitely many.
nodes.title: Number of maximal independent sets

nodes.summary: Let $f_{\max}(G)$ be the number of maximal sum-free subsets of $G$. As $k \to \infty$, with $n = 2^k$, $f_{\max}(\mathbb{Z}_2^k) = \bigl(\binom{n-1}{2} + o(1)\bigr) 2^{n/4}$, and with $n = 3^k$, $f_{\max}(\mathbb{Z}_3^k) = \bigl((n-3)(n-1)/3 + o(1)\bigr) 3^{n/9}$; that is, $f_{\max}(\mathbb{Z}_2^k)/2^{n/4} - \binom{n-1}{2} \to 0$ and $f_{\max}(\mathbb{Z}_3^k)/3^{n/9} - (n-3)(n-1)/3 \to 0$.
nodes.title: Counting maximal sum-free sets in elementary abelian 2- and 3-groups

nodes.summary: For a set $G$ with an addition, $f_{\max}(G)$ is the number of maximal sum-free subsets of $G$, that is, of sets $S \subseteq G$ with $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$ (including $x = y$) that are not properly contained in another such set; it is $0$ if there are infinitely many.
nodes.title: Number of maximal sum-free sets

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $B, S \subseteq G$ be disjoint distinct sum-free sets. If $I \subseteq B$ and $S \cup I$ is a maximal distinct sum-free subset of $G$, then $I$ is a maximal independent set of the distinct link graph $L^*_S[B]$: a subset of $B$ with no looped vertex and no two adjacent vertices that is not properly contained in another such set.
nodes.title: Link-graph extension lemma

nodes.summary: In a finite abelian group $G$, for every natural number $k$ the number of subgroups of order $k$ equals the number of subgroups of index $k$.
nodes.title: Counting subgroups by order and by index

nodes.title: Ranks of the index-two subgroups of a finite abelian 2-group

nodes.title: Random sum-free sets

Call $S \subseteq G$ sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$, and distinct sum-free if $x + y \notin S$ for all $x, y \in S$ such that $x$, $y$ and $x + y$ are pairwise distinct. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
